summary.text: Weakly interacting massive particles, or WIMPs, are hypothetical particles proposed as a candidate for dark matter.
They would have mass and interact through gravity, but being invisible to normal observation and weakly interacting, they would be extremely hard to detect.
Experiments have searched for them for years, and as of 2026 none of these efforts has succeeded.

facts.label: Dark matter type
facts.value: Cold: heavy and slow-moving, so they clump together

facts.label: Other candidates
facts.value: Massive compact halo objects and axions

facts.label: Proposed
facts.value: Suggested a decade after the 1970s dark matter problem

facts.label: Neutrinos
facts.value: Very light and fast, so counted as hot

items.prompt: Why are WIMPs called cold dark matter instead of hot?

options.label: Because they give off almost no heat at all
Because they are very light, like neutrinos
Because they only exist at low temperatures
Because their large mass makes them relatively slow moving

items.explain: Because of their large mass, WIMPs would move relatively slowly and so be "cold".

items.prompt: A friend suggests neutrinos could be the cold dark matter, since they barely interact with ordinary matter. What is wrong with that?

options.label: They are very light and so move fast, making them hot
They interact strongly with normal matter
They are heavier than WIMPs and move slowly
They clump together too easily

items.explain: Particles that interact little with normal matter, such as neutrinos, are very light and fast moving, or hot.

items.prompt: If dark matter were hot, what would happen to the pattern of galaxies?

options.label: Large-scale structure would be smeared out
Galaxies would form faster into tight clumps
Nothing would change in the pattern
Galaxies would be arranged on straight lines

items.explain: Hot dark matter would smear out the large-scale structure of galaxies, so it is not considered a viable model.

items.prompt: Researchers look at the centres of galaxies and small satellite galaxies of the Milky Way for signs of WIMPs. Why choose small satellite galaxies?

options.label: They are the closest objects to our planet
They have the greatest number of stars of all
They hold very little ordinary matter, so less background
They are the only places where WIMPs can exist

items.explain: They tend to contain very little baryonic matter, reducing the expected background from standard astrophysical processes.

items.prompt: What kind of signal do typical indirect searches look for?

options.label: Visible light flashes in deep space
Sound waves from collisions
Heat radiating from empty regions
Excess gamma rays from annihilation or related processes

items.explain: Typical indirect searches look for excess gamma rays, predicted as products of annihilation or produced when charged particles interact with ambient radiation.

items.prompt: Why has the lack of evidence for supersymmetry at the Large Hadron Collider hurt WIMP hopes?

options.label: It proved that dark matter does not exist
It cast doubt on the simplest WIMP hypotheses
It showed WIMPs are too heavy to detect
It made WIMPs no longer a candidate at all

items.explain: Supersymmetric extensions readily predict WIMP particles, so the lack of evidence cast doubt on these simplest WIMP hypotheses.
